caption: The drawing depicts a large, ornate baptismal font made of what appears to be stone or marble. The font is primarily painted in light pink and beige tones with gray areas at the top and base. It has a wide bowl with a rounded body tapering to a narrower base. Around the upper part of the font, there are decorative garlands painted in red, green, and blue with blue, red, and yellow flowers interspersed. The word "SAN LUIS REY" is inscribed in red letters around the neck of the font. The base is decorated with gray and orange swirling patterns. The font has a broken or chipped edge on the upper right side, revealing a small inset basin filled with blue water. Resting on top of the font is a brownish-gold, dome-shaped metal lid decorated with embossed patterns, a latch, and a cross at the top. The illustration includes subtle shading and detail lines, indicating light falling from the upper left and casting a shadow on the right side of the object. A thin dark border frames the drawing, and text at the bottom left reads "HOWARD H. SHERMAN '36". The overall composition is centered, and the objects are rendered in a realistic style.
title: Baptismal Font at San Luis Rey Mission Church
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
